Reasoned review of 5b2592637390, 0bad645c0037 and 03b12f133dd1
2026-10-25

All three originals were analyzed with atomscan and cleave facts. PE code was
disassembled, not executed. Analysis artifacts and Forager provenance are in
scratch/fallout-review/current. The original SHA-256 values were verified
before writing the verdict markers.

5b2592637390: BENIGN -- Bitwarden iOS source archive

The submitted archive is ios-main (6,256 TAR entries), not gh-actions itself.
Its _build-any.yml references bitwarden/gh-actions. The submitted TAR contains
no symlinks. The two reported suspicious finding occurrences belong to the
fetched gh-actions dependency and its nested unzip-stream fixture, respectively.

The dependency was independently scanned before and after with:
  SCAN_FOLLOW=none atomscan purl pkg:github/bitwarden/gh-actions@main
      --no-update --analyze local -f json
Its immutable analyzed SHA-256 is
edc9c0f6db2848527125c2481f6fb606d49fd019b4603110c48d7982a7a90119.
Forager's explicit refs/heads/main URL recovered exactly these bytes, with
provenance; its PURL tag URL first returned 404. No reconstructed archive was
substituted for the dependency.

download-artifacts vendors unzip-stream 0.3.1. Its testData-golang/symlink.zip
(SHA-256 c871234a8d0c8787eacb357e53245d6663803fef1750518204a1aa97ec321f62)
is 173 bytes and contains one mode-0120777 entry named symlink, whose data is
../target. It contains no executable payload or follow-on write through that
link. The package's test harness streams ZIP entries into its parser; package
metadata declares tap ./test/*.js. This is a parser regression corpus. The
escape observation is nevertheless physically correct, so both suspicious
occurrences are retained. No dependent-package exception or fixture-name
exclusion was added.

The original's current classifier flag instead traces to two Swift members
with probability 1.0: IdentityTokenResponseModel+Fixtures.swift and WatchApp's
CryptoService.swift. The first constructs test authentication responses with
example values, an expired JWT and @testable imports. The second generates or
loads this application's AES key from its own Keychain entry, encrypts and
decrypts local data, and deletes that entry on clearKey. These paths establish
neither credential theft nor ransomware. The extension's page collection and
fill callbacks implement its password-manager purpose. The pyeetd build helper
lists processes and kills explicitly selected simulator/OS background tasks.
These capabilities remain detected. No deployment or signing evidence for a
compiled app is supplied by a source archive; the verdict concerns these bytes.

0bad645c0037: MALICIOUS -- VB6 Blackshades RAT server

The PE entry at 0x4013bc enters MSVBVM60 with VBHeader 0x401d84. ProjectInfo
0x4032d0 has no native-code address; its 40 objects expose 554 recovered p-code
procedures. Native-only disassembly initially misidentified bytecode as x86.
VB object/method/constant-pool parsing and opcode decoding recovered actual
calls, constants and branches. The parser is recorded as vb-disassemble.py.
API thunks were resolved through their Declare descriptors and IAT entries.

Decisive execution paths include:
* Keyboard-hook installer 0x43ba24 passes WH_KEYBOARD_LL=13 and a callback to
  SetWindowsHookExA. Callback 0x44728c handles keydown, invokes Unicode key
  translation at 0x454540, collects foreground-window titles at 0x446c8c and
  concatenates them and keys into buffers. GetAsyncKeyState helpers alone read
  shift keys; describing the entire recorder as polling misses its main hook.
* Received-command dispatch at 0x4676d0 splits packet fields and branches on
  commands. At 0x46983d one branch calls the audio recorder at 0x453ae8. The
  recorder issues waveaudio open/format/record commands through mciSendStringA;
  0x44eda0 stops and saves the recording. These are called paths, not merely
  microphone strings.
* 0x43a8a4 assembles REG ADD commands that allow firewall exceptions and add an
  enabled wildcard-scope application rule with a misleading Windows Messenger
  label, then calls VB Shell (ordinal 600). The existing registry-tamper rule
  remains supported; its low-level registry API evidence is also real.
* 0x457d78 conditionally registers configured image paths under Explorer policy
  Run and CurrentVersion Run keys and Active Setup StubPath for HKLM/HKCU.
  0x449968 builds argument arrays for RegCreateKeyA and RegSetValueExA through
  the dynamic API dispatcher. Configuration and operator tasks gate these
  capabilities; static analysis does not assert successful installation.

Obfuscation was decoded offline. The SETTINGS resource is ASCII hex. After
hex decoding, its first 32 bytes are a key; CRC32(key) is 0x47fe7f1a. modENC
computes that CRC, executes Rnd(-1), seeds Randomize with the CRC, and XORs
each remaining byte with Int(Rnd()*256). The recovered configuration contains
fw.crashtm.org, command/transfer ports 1902/1903, and an executable install
name. decode-vb-config.py records the replay. Microsoft's implementation
explicitly documents equivalence with the VB6 random routines:
https://source.dot.net/Microsoft.VisualBasic.Core/Microsoft/VisualBasic/VBMath.vb.html

A separate hex/repeating-key XOR routine at 0x442d80 conceals the Run-key
paths. Replaying its shifted modulo indexing with the supplied key recovers
SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run and the Explorer policy Run key.
The new XOR reconstruction matcher requires its arithmetic/call/character-XOR
sequence without requiring a key, endpoint, project name or file basename.

The project's Blackshades attribution agrees with four independent existing
family signatures, but the verdict rests on remotely tasked surveillance and
unwanted durability/security changes. The rival-RAT names and KaZaA registry
string also occur in bot-killer detection code; they were not treated as proof
that this specimen implements every named rival's features. Authorized research
or administration context on a receiving machine is unknown.

03b12f133dd1: MALICIOUS -- DataClass process-hollowing helper

All CLR method bodies were disassembled with dnfile/dncil, resolving method
tokens, delegates and user strings. Generated My/resources boilerplate does
not supply independent attack behaviors. DataClass.InputData.StartData, RVA
0x230c, accepts image bytes and a host command line. Its resolver at RVA 0x22d8
uses LoadLibraryA/GetProcAddress/GetDelegateForFunctionPointer on Base64-decoded
API names. The trace establishes:
* CIL 0x1c3..0x1d9 calls CreateProcessA with CREATE_SUSPENDED=4.
* It obtains thread context, reads the remote image base, and calls
  ZwUnmapViewOfSection to remove the original image.
* 0x2b3..0x2cc allocates remote memory with MEM_COMMIT|MEM_RESERVE and
  PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE. It writes headers and each section of the supplied
  PE, changes the remote image-base pointer and entry-register context, then
  sets context and resumes the primary thread at 0x41e..0x42c.

The encoded APIs and full replacement of another image tip the balance toward
malicious payload concealment. The unsigned Microsoft version fields supply
no trustworthy provenance. No deployment authorization or payload supplied to
this DLL is present in this individual sample; neither was invented. SOAP and
resource-management boilerplate is not evidence of a network control channel.

Added encoded ReadProcessMemory and Base64 WriteProcessMemory observations and
encoded process-API/delegate concealment. The unpadded WriteProcessMemory
spelling is misclassified as Base58 by the generic string decoder, so the
neutral atom matches its actual Base64 text. The existing hollowing detections
remain unchanged.

Coverage goal: this DLL has one independently supported hostile effect,
process hollowing. Its API concealment is now suspicious coverage, not a
second or third hostile copy of the same injection. Full IL review found no
independent persistence, stealing, destruction or C2 implementation to support
3--5 hostile traits. There is no hidden extracted stage left unexamined in
this helper, and no family/hash rule was added to manufacture extra coverage.

Rule correction, consumers and controls

The old vb6-runtime-windowproc-process-scan matcher required only VB runtime,
CallWindowProc, memory copying, GetProcAddress and Process32Next references.
In this specimen the subclass/socket thunk implementation accounts for the
window-procedure machinery; the required set establishes no static-concealment
mechanism. It moved, with identical required legs and PE/Windows scope, to
micro-behaviors/process/enumerate/snapshot::vb6-windowproc-process-api-profile
at notable. The generic T1027 mapping was removed. This retains its supported
observation while correcting the unsupported obfuscation inference.

The exact vb6-single-host-image-file-infector consumer now requires the new
ID. Ancestor selectors were inspected: process-enumeration consumers already
receive the required Process32Next atom, and use the directory as one all-leg,
so the added profile cannot supply a missing independent role. Two broad
imports-obfuscation exclusions (debugger-check aggregation and oversized rdata)
no longer accept this neutral API profile as evidence of concealment. They
retain their other import-concealment exclusions. No attack matcher was deleted.

verify.py checks five mutation/positive cases without executing samples:
removing StubPath removes only the new persistence inference; changing hook
type 13 removes the new keyboard-recorder inference; changing encoded
CreateProcessA removes encoded-resolution/hollowing inferences. Positive
specimens retain their detections. Three checked-in artifacts outside this
batch (benign crashpad input, benign keylog/dropper control, hostile native
directory-hide hook) have identical complete before/after finding sets.
The relocation's original legs and exact consumer are also checked. Results
are in controls.json. The hostile persistence precision is 8.8, above the
3.5 authoring floor; precision diagnostics did not establish the verdict.

Before/after scan comparison

H/S counts are finding occurrences over each scan's original and members.
The gh-actions count includes its parent and nested fixture; it is one
physical escaping symlink, not two independent attack behaviors.

Artifact                              Before H/S  After H/S   Classifier
Bitwarden iOS local source                  0/0        0/0     flagged -> flagged
gh-actions dependency in isolation          0/2        0/2     unflagged -> unflagged
VB6 Blackshades server                      6/5        7/5     flagged -> flagged
DataClass DLL                              1/1        1/2     unflagged -> unflagged

comparison.json records probabilities, calibrated levels, hashes and all H/S
IDs. lvl=-1 denotes an unflagged result even when probability is high. The
original iOS source remains a classifier false positive, and DataClass remains
a classifier miss despite correct hostile hollowing coverage. The engine also
warns that model v18 uses an older feature specification than its current
extractor. No rule was inflated or duplicated to influence those decisions.

The only removed original finding ID is the relocated neutral VB6 API profile;
its supported observation remains. No hostile finding was lost. The first
archive invocation also returned 15 optional registry-popularity sidecars;
the normalized local comparison excludes those fetched registry records,
which are not members or code detections. No relevant trait was weakened to
clear the Bitwarden archive or its dependency.

Verdict-marker/commit-body lines:
Bitwarden iOS: benign source; ZIP escape is a parser fixture
Blackshades RAT: keylogging, audio capture and startup registration
DataClass DLL: suspended-image replacement with encoded APIs

The final required action is make validate; its result is reported separately.
